reply.text:
On 9 December 2022, the Council adopted Resolution 2664 by 14 votes in favour, with India abstaining. The US and Ireland introduced the draft. The resolution preserves underlying asset-freeze obligations while exempting qualifying actors from providing or processing resources necessary for timely humanitarian assistance or basic human needs. This two-year exemption for ISIL and Al-Qaida regimes includes due diligence requirements to minimize prohibited benefits, monitored by the 1267 Committee with expert support.

India objected, warning of diversion risks and urging proactive 1267 Monitoring Team involvement and robust reporting standards. It judged these specific concerns not fully addressed in the adopted text. The Council's safeguards aim to balance oversight with operational flexibility, though India felt the resolution failed to resolve its identified gaps regarding monitoring and reporting mechanisms.
